description: The bar chart titled “Runtime Comparison of Models in Streaming Environment” visually compares the inference runtime (in seconds) of five different models under a streaming setup. The vertical axis represents runtime in seconds, ranging from 0 to 400 with major gridlines at 50-second intervals. The horizontal axis lists five models: “Our Joint Framework,” “ChatGPT,” “DeepSeek,” “LLaMA,” and “Claude.” A legend in the top-left corner indicates that “Our Joint Framework” is represented by a dark green bar, while “LLM Models” are shown in light blue — though in practice, all LLMs (ChatGPT, DeepSeek, LLaMA, Claude) are displayed as light blue bars, and “Our Joint Framework” is the only green bar. The runtime values are labeled directly above each bar: “Our Joint Framework” achieves 77 seconds, significantly faster than the LLMs; ChatGPT takes 190 seconds, DeepSeek 365 seconds (the slowest), LLaMA 172 seconds, and Claude 243 seconds. The chart visually emphasizes the efficiency of “Our Joint Framework” by placing it first and using a distinct color, while the LLMs are grouped together in light blue, showing a wide variation in their performance. The chart does not include error bars or statistical significance indicators, and the bars are not sorted by runtime — instead, “Our Joint Framework” is positioned first, followed by the LLMs in what appears to be alphabetical or arbitrary order. This visualization supports the paper’s claim of improved efficiency in detecting fraud and concept drift in online conversations using their proposed joint framework compared to standalone LLMs.
